requirements: fd >= 0 assigns and takes ownership; fd < 0 clears to an empty (-1) state (documented in code comments/logic).
file may be NULL; when non-NULL, it is used for logging (documented by usage).
Callers should not rely on errno being modified by this function; it preserves errno (documented in comments).

functions.name: Passenger::FileDescriptor::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assignment operator. Makes this FileDescriptor share ownership of the same underlying fd as other via reference counting. Preserves errno across the assignment.
requirements: Be aware that after assignment, both objects refer to the same fd; closing via either will close the shared fd for all copies (inferred from class description).
Callers should not rely on errno being modified by this operation; it preserves errno (documented in comments).

functions.name: Passenger::FileDescriptorPair::operator[]
functions.description: Indexed access to the two elements of the FileDescriptorPair. Index 0 returns the first FileDescriptor; index 1 returns the second. Any other index throws ArgumentException.
requirements: index must be 0 or 1; otherwise an ArgumentException is thrown (explicitly enforced in code).

functions.name: Passenger::EventFd::notify
functions.description: Signals the EventFd by writing a single byte to the internal writer end of its pipe. Intended to be used to wake a thread that is select()/poll()ing on fd(). Throws SystemException if the write fails with an error other than EAGAIN.
requirements: Callers must handle SystemException on write failure when errno != EAGAIN (explicit in code).
This function is safe to call from another thread to wake a thread waiting on fd() (documented in class comment).

functions.name: Passenger::EventFd::fd
functions.description: Returns the read end (reader) file descriptor of the internal pipe. Use this with select()/poll()/epoll to wait for notifications.
requirements: The returned descriptor is a POSIX file descriptor suitable for readiness-based I/O APIs (documented purpose).

functions.name: Passenger::EventFd::writerFd
functions.description: Returns the write end (writer) file descriptor of the internal pipe. Primarily used internally by notify(), but exposed for advanced use cases.
requirements: The returned descriptor is a POSIX file descriptor for writing a single-byte notification as used by notify() (inferred from implementation).

functions.name: Passenger::runSingleHookScript
functions.signature: inline bool Passenger::runSingleHookScript(Passenger::HookScriptOptions &options, const std::string &command, const std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> &envvars)
functions.description: Execute a single hook script command as a subprocess, setting environment variables provided via envvars. Logs start, errors, and non-zero exit statuses, and returns true only if the subprocess status is 0 or -2 (the latter treated as success by this implementation; precise meaning unknown). Intended to be used by higher-level hook execution that prepares command and environment based on HookScriptOptions.
requirements: options.name should be set to a non-empty identifier for logging and for inclusion in PASSENGER_HOOK_NAME when used by higher-level helpers (required by HookScriptOptions contract).
command must be a non-empty string naming an executable or command that runCommand can launch; providing an invalid or non-existent command will cause the function to log an error and return false.
envvars must contain valid environment variable name/value pairs (names must be acceptable to setenv; values are arbitrary strings).
Caller should check the boolean return value; false indicates the command failed to run or did not exit with an accepted status.
This function may modify environment variables in the spawned process context via a callback; callers should not assume parent process environment is changed.

functions.name: Passenger::runHookScripts
functions.description: Parse and execute a sequence of hook script commands defined in options.spec. The spec is split on ';' and each command is trimmed. Builds an environment for the hook scripts from options.agentConfig and options.environment and adds PASSENGER_HOOK_NAME. Executes each command in order; stops and returns false on the first failure. Returns true if no spec is provided, the parsed list is empty, or all commands succeed.
requirements: options.spec should be a semicolon-separated list of commands; empty spec results in a no-op that returns true.
options.name is required (used to set PASSENGER_HOOK_NAME in the environment for each script and for logging).

options.agentConfig, if provided, is converted to environment variables with keys prefixed by PASSENGER_; non-string values are serialized via toStyledString; the key PASSENGER_CONFIG_MANIFEST is skipped.

options.environment may supply additional environment variable pairs; later entries override earlier ones only if duplicate names are present when applied by the child process environment setting callback.
Caller must handle the boolean return value; false means at least one script failed to execute successfully.
Commands are executed sequentially; a failure in any command prevents subsequent commands from running.

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::InstanceDirectory
functions.description: Constructs a new instance directory under the system temporary directory using a unique path derived from options.prefix. It creates and initializes the directory structure and metadata (properties.json, subdirectories, and lock file). Intended for creating and owning a fresh instance directory for the current process. Throws on filesystem errors or if a unique directory cannot be created.
requirements: options must describe valid creation parameters; if running as root and options.userSwitching is false, options.defaultUid and options.defaultGid should be valid IDs for chown when creating apps.s (inferred from code)
The process must have permission to create directories and files in the system temporary directory (usually returned by getSystemTempDir())
On error, exceptions such as Passenger::RuntimeException or Passenger::FileSystemException may be thrown; callers must be prepared to handle exceptions

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::InstanceDirectory
functions.description: Constructs a new instance directory inside the specified registryDir using a unique path derived from options.prefix. It initializes required structure and metadata. Use when you need instance directories under a specific parent directory.
requirements: registryDir must exist and be writable/executable by the effective user so that a subdirectory can be created and chowned/chmodded
options must describe valid creation parameters; if running as root and options.userSwitching is false, options.defaultUid and options.defaultGid should be valid IDs (used for apps.s)
On error, exceptions such as Passenger::RuntimeException or Passenger::FileSystemException may be thrown; callers must be prepared to handle exceptions

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::InstanceDirectory
functions.description: Wraps an existing instance directory path without taking ownership for automatic destruction. Use to reference an already-created instance directory. No initialization is performed.
requirements: dir must refer to an existing, valid instance directory structure if the caller intends to use it as such (not validated by constructor)

Caller is responsible for lifecycle; the instance will not be automatically removed on destruction unless destroy() is called after switching to owner via design not provided (this instance is non-owner by default)

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::~InstanceDirectory
functions.description: Destructor. If this object is marked as the owner of the instance directory, it removes the directory tree; otherwise it leaves the directory intact. Ownership can be released via detach().
requirements: If owner is true at destruction, the directory tree at getPath() will be removed; callers should ensure no other process/thread relies on it when the object goes out of scope
If you do not want automatic removal, call detach() before destruction

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::finalizeCreation
functions.description: Marks the instance directory as fully created by writing an empty creation_finalized file in the instance directory. Intended to signal that initialization is complete.
requirements: Must be called only when this object is the owner; in debug builds, calling when not owner triggers an assertion failure
Caller must have write permissions in the instance directory; otherwise an exception from file creation may be thrown

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::getPath
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the instance directory path. Useful for passing to components that need the path without copying.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the InstanceDirectory object exists; do not store the reference beyond the object's lifetime
The caller must not modify the underlying string (const reference)

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::detach
functions.description: Releases ownership so the destructor will not remove the instance directory. Use before destruction when you want to keep the directory.
requirements: After calling detach(), destroy() will still assert owner in debug builds; do not call destroy() after detaching unless ownership is transferred back by other means (not provided)

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::isOwner
functions.description: Returns whether this object currently owns the instance directory (i.e., whether it will remove it on destruction and is allowed to destroy it).
requirements: None

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::destroy
functions.description: Recursively removes the instance directory and its contents, and clears ownership so it will not be removed again. Use to explicitly tear down the directory.
requirements: Must be called only when this object is the owner; in debug builds, calling when not owner triggers an assertion failure
Caller must ensure no other process/thread needs the directory or files when invoked
Requires permissions to remove all files and subdirectories inside the instance directory; on failure, exceptions may be thrown by removal routines

functions.name: Passenger::InstanceDirectory::generateInstanceId
functions.description: Generates a unique, human-readable instance ID combining the current time (hexatri format) and two random 6-character ASCII strings. Use when you need to label or correlate instance directories or processes.
requirements: None

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::RandomGenerator
functions.description: Constructs a RandomGenerator that reads cryptographically secure random data from /dev/urandom. If open is true (default) the constructor immediately opens /dev/urandom and caches the handle; if false, no device is opened until reopen() is called. Intended for repeated random generation without re-opening the device each time.
requirements: If open is true, the constructor may throw Passenger::FileSystemException if /dev/urandom cannot be opened; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.
open=false can be used to defer opening; in that case, generate*() methods must not be called until reopen() has successfully completed.
Underlying platform must provide a readable /dev/urandom.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::~RandomGenerator
functions.description: Destructor that closes the cached /dev/urandom handle if open. Uses LoggingKit to log descriptor close and ignores fclose errors. Thread interruption is disabled during close.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.
No specific caller-side error handling is required; the destructor does not propagate exceptions.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::reopen
functions.description: Closes any currently open /dev/urandom handle and opens a new one, caching the FILE* for subsequent reads. Useful after fork or if the handle has been closed.
requirements: Must not be called concurrently with close() from other threads (class is thread-safe except during concurrent reopen/close).
May throw Passenger::FileSystemException if /dev/urandom cannot be opened; callers must handle this exception.
Underlying platform must provide a readable /dev/urandom.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::close
functions.description: Closes the cached /dev/urandom handle if it is open. Safe to call multiple times; a no-op if not open. Logs descriptor close.
requirements: Must not be called concurrently with reopen() from other threads (class is thread-safe except during concurrent reopen/close).
After close(), generate*() methods must not be called until reopen() successfully opens the device again.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateBytes
functions.description: Fills the provided buffer with size bytes of cryptographically secure random data read from /dev/urandom and returns a StaticString view over that buffer. Intended when the caller supplies storage.
requirements: handle must be open (constructor with open=true or a prior successful reopen()); otherwise behavior will result in an exception.
buf must point to writable memory of at least size bytes; if size > 0, buf must be non-null.
On short read or read failure, throws Passenger::IOException; callers must handle this exception.
The returned Passenger::StaticString references the caller-provided memory; the buffer must outlive any use of the StaticString.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateByteString
functions.description: Allocates and returns a std::string of length size filled with random bytes from /dev/urandom. Suitable for binary data; contents are not null-terminated beyond the std::string's managed storage.
requirements: handle must be open (via constructor or reopen()).
May throw Passenger::IOException on read failure; callers must handle this exception.
size may be zero to obtain an empty string.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateHexString
functions.description: Generates size random bytes and returns their hexadecimal string representation. Useful for IDs or tokens. Note: based on typical toHex behavior, the returned string length will be 2*size (inferred from naming).
requirements: handle must be open (via constructor or reopen()).
May throw Passenger::IOException on read failure; callers must handle this exception.
size may be zero to obtain an empty string (likely zero-length hex output).

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateAsciiString
functions.description: Returns a std::string of length size consisting only of ASCII alphanumeric characters [A-Za-z0-9], derived from random bytes. Distribution is slightly non-uniform as documented in the comment (a–i have 5/256 chance; others 4/256).
requirements: handle must be open (via constructor or reopen()).
May throw Passenger::IOException on read failure via internal generateBytes(); callers must handle this exception.
size may be zero to obtain an empty string.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateAsciiString
functions.description: Fills the provided buffer with size ASCII alphanumeric characters [A-Za-z0-9], derived from random bytes. Distribution is slightly non-uniform as documented in the comment.
requirements: handle must be open (via constructor or reopen()).
_buf must point to writable memory of at least size bytes; if size > 0, _buf must be non-null.
May throw Passenger::IOException on read failure via internal generateBytes(); callers must handle this exception.
The function does not append a null terminator; if a C-string is desired, the caller must ensure space for and placement of a terminator.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateInt
functions.description: Returns a random int filled with cryptographically secure random bytes from /dev/urandom. No range constraints; full bit pattern of int is possible.
requirements: handle must be open (via constructor or reopen()).
May throw Passenger::IOException on read failure via internal generateBytes(); callers must handle this exception.
Be aware of platform endianness and sign; if a non-negative range is required, use generateUint() or post-process.

functions.name: Passenger::RandomGenerator::generateUint
functions.description: Returns a random unsigned int by reinterpreting the bits of a random int as unsigned. Useful when a non-negative random integer is desired.
requirements: handle must be open (via constructor or reopen()).
May throw Passenger::IOException on read failure via internal generateBytes(); callers must handle this exception.
Returned value spans the full range of unsigned int; no upper-bound guarantee beyond the type width.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::ResourceLocator
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty ResourceLocator with no initialization beyond default-initialized members. Typically followed by assignment or use of the non-default constructor for proper configuration.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::ResourceLocator
functions.description: Constructs a ResourceLocator from an install specification. If _installSpec names a regular file, it is treated as an INI file and the 'locations' section is read to determine resource paths. Otherwise, _installSpec is treated as the root of a source/build tree and standard subdirectories are derived.
requirements: If _installSpec refers to a regular file, it must be a readable INI file with a 'locations' section containing keys: packaging_method, bin_dir, support_binaries_dir, helper_scripts_dir, resources_dir, doc_dir, ruby_libdir, node_libdir.
Missing required keys in the INI file cause a RuntimeException to be thrown.
When _installSpec is not a regular file, it is treated as a directory-like root; no validation of subpaths is performed by this constructor.
Callers should be prepared to handle exceptions thrown by INI parsing (e.g., missing sections/keys) or filesystem queries.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::isOriginallyPackaged
functions.description: Indicates whether this locator was initialized from a non-regular install spec (treated as a packaged source/build tree) rather than an INI file. Useful to distinguish packaged vs. configured installs.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getInstallSpec
functions.description: Returns the original install specification used to construct this locator. For INI-based initialization, this is the INI file path; otherwise, the root directory path.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getPackagingMethod
functions.description: Returns the packaging method string. Set from the INI file when initialized from a file, or 'unknown' when initialized from a root directory.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getBinDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the Passenger bin directory as determined during construction.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getSupportBinariesDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the directory containing support binaries.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getUserSupportBinariesDir
functions.description: Returns the per-user directory path for support binaries for the current Passenger version (based on the user's home directory and constants).

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getHelperScriptsDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the directory containing helper scripts.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getResourcesDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the resources directory.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getDocDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the documentation directory.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getRubyLibDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the Ruby support library directory.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getNodeLibDir
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the Node.js support library directory.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::getBuildSystemDir
functions.description: Returns the build system root directory path. May be empty when initialized from an INI file.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the ResourceLocator object remains alive.
Callers must handle the possibility that the returned string is empty.

functions.name: Passenger::ResourceLocator::findSupportBinary
functions.description: Locates a support binary by name. Searches the system-wide support binaries directory first; if not found, searches the per-user support binaries directory for the current version. Returns the first matching absolute path or throws if not found.
requirements: The input parameter 'name' should correspond to a filename (no path separators recommended).
Callers must handle RuntimeException when the binary is not found.
A SystemException from a filesystem check may propagate for the user directory lookup; callers should be prepared to handle it.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new watchdog launcher handle for starting the Passenger watchdog/agents, configured for the specified integration mode. Use with the C API functions to start, query, detach, and free the launcher. If allocation or setup fails, the function returns NULL and may set an error message.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid PsgIntegrationMode value (IM_APACHE, IM_NGINX, or IM_STANDALONE).
Returned PsgWatchdogLauncher* must be released with psg_watchdog_launcher_free() when no longer needed.
Behavior and lifetime of the string at *error_message (allocation, ownership, and whether it may be NULL) are unknown; consult implementation or higher-level docs.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_start
functions.signature: int psg_watchdog_launcher_start(PsgWatchdogLauncher *launcher, const char *passengerRoot, PsgJsonValue *config, const PsgAfterForkCallback afterFork, void *callbackArgument, char **errorMessage);
functions.description: Starts the Passenger watchdog (and associated agents) using the provided launcher, Passenger root path, and optional JSON configuration. Optionally invokes an after-fork callback in the child process just before exec. On success, the launcher becomes associated with the running watchdog, and the getter functions can be used to retrieve connection details and PID.
requirements: launcher must be a non-NULL pointer returned by psg_watchdog_launcher_new() and not yet started.
passengerRoot must be a non-NULL path to a valid Passenger installation root containing the required agent executable; exact validation rules are unknown.
config is expected to reference a JSON value understood by the library; exact schema is unknown.

afterFork, if non-NULL, will be called in the forked child process after resetting signal handlers/mask and before exec; it receives (callbackArgument, NULL) per typedef. It should perform only safe operations for a post-fork, pre-exec context; exact constraints are not documented here.
error handling contract (return value meaning, population and ownership of *errorMessage) is unknown; caller must check the return value and, on failure, inspect errorMessage if provided.
May not be called more than once per launcher instance; behavior of repeated calls is undefined.
Must not be used concurrently from multiple threads unless higher-level docs guarantee thread-safety.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_get_core_address
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an internal, NUL-terminated string containing the address where the Passenger core listens for HTTP requests. Intended for use after a successful start. Optionally returns the string length via size.
requirements: launcher must be a valid, started launcher (i.e., psg_watchdog_launcher_start succeeded and the launcher has not been detached or freed).
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; lifetime and thread-safety are unknown. Do not free it.
Meaning and inclusion/exclusion of the NUL terminator in *size are unknown.
Behavior when size is NULL is unknown.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_get_core_password
functions.description: Returns the password string required to authenticate with the Passenger core. Intended for use after a successful start. Optionally returns the string length via size.
requirements: launcher must be a valid, started launcher (i.e., psg_watchdog_launcher_start succeeded and the launcher has not been detached or freed).
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; lifetime and thread-safety are unknown. Do not free it.
Meaning and inclusion/exclusion of the NUL terminator in *size are unknown.
Behavior when size is NULL is unknown.
Treat this value as sensitive; how to securely handle it is not specified here.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_get_instance_dir
functions.description: Returns the path to the instance directory created by the watchdog. Intended for use after a successful start. Optionally returns the string length via size.
requirements: launcher must be a valid, started launcher (i.e., psg_watchdog_launcher_start succeeded and the launcher has not been detached or freed).
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; lifetime and thread-safety are unknown. Do not free it.
Meaning and inclusion/exclusion of the NUL terminator in *size are unknown.
Behavior when size is NULL is unknown.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_get_pid
functions.description: Returns the PID of the watchdog process associated with the launcher. Returns 0 if the watchdog has not been started or after the launcher has been detached.
requirements: launcher must be a non-NULL pointer to a launcher object.
The returned PID reflects the current state tracked by the launcher; after detach it will be 0.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_detach
functions.description: Detaches the launcher from the running watchdog, closing any internal file descriptors and preventing the launcher from attempting a clean shutdown in its destructor/free. After detaching, getters will no longer be valid and get_pid will report 0.
requirements: launcher must be a non-NULL pointer to a launcher object.
After detaching, do not use the getter functions that return strings; their data is no longer valid.
Detach does not free the launcher; the caller must still call psg_watchdog_launcher_free() to release the object.
If a watchdog is running, it will continue independently; lifecycle control after detach is outside this API.

functions.name: psg_watchdog_launcher_free
functions.description: Frees the launcher object and releases any associated resources. If still attached to a running watchdog, behavior is implementation-defined; typically the launcher would attempt to notify and wait during destruction unless previously detached.
requirements: launcher may be NULL or non-NULL; whether NULL is accepted is unknown.
After calling, the launcher pointer must not be used again.
If the launcher was not detached, freeing may attempt a clean shutdown; exact semantics are unknown.

functions.name: Passenger::WatchdogLauncher::getIntegrationModeString
functions.description: Returns a string literal indicating the integration mode for which the launcher was constructed: "apache", "nginx", "standalone", or "unknown" for unspecified values.
requirements: Method may be called at any time on a valid WatchdogLauncher instance.
Returned pointer refers to a static string literal; do not free.

functions.name: Passenger::WatchdogLauncher::start
functions.signature: void Passenger::WatchdogLauncher::start(const std::string &passengerRoot, const Json::Value &extraConfig = Json::Value(), const boost::function<void ()> &afterFork = boost::function<void ()>());
functions.description: Starts the Passenger watchdog (and agents) via fork/exec of the support binary (AGENT_EXE), passing configuration over a feedback channel. On success, records the watchdog PID and exposes the core address, core password, and instance directory. Optionally executes a user-provided callback in the forked child just before exec. Throws on failure with detailed diagnostics.
requirements: passengerRoot must identify a valid Passenger installation root where the watchdog/agent support binary can be located; otherwise a RuntimeException/SystemException is thrown.
extraConfig should be a JSON object of additional configuration; keys override defaults merged with internal config; exact schema is not documented here.

afterFork, if provided, will be called in the forked child process after resetting signal handlers/mask, after setting PASSENGER_USE_FEEDBACK_FD, and before closing all FDs (except stdin, stdout, stderr, and feedback fd) and before exec; it must not rely on threads or unsafe post-fork operations; throwing from afterFork is unspecified and should be avoided.
This method throws on errors (SystemException, IOException, RuntimeException) and never returns partial success.
Do not call start() more than once per WatchdogLauncher instance; call detach() or destroy and recreate a launcher if needed.
Not safe to call concurrently on the same instance.

functions.name: Passenger::WatchdogLauncher::detach
functions.description: Closes internal file descriptors and prevents the destructor from attempting a clean shutdown of the watchdog. Postcondition: getPid() == 0. The watchdog, if running, continues independently.
requirements: May be called after a successful start; has no effect on an instance that was never started.
After calling, do not use members that rely on the feedback channel or stored core address/password/instance dir.
Thread-safety is not specified; avoid concurrent calls.

functions.name: Passenger::parseAppLocalConfigFile
functions.description: Parses the application-local configuration file Passengerfile.json located under the given application root and returns a minimal AppLocalConfig containing only safe, non-sensitive fields. Specifically reads app_start_command (string) and app_supports_kuria_protocol (bool). If the file does not exist, returns defaults (empty appStartCommand, appSupportsKuriaProtocol=false). Enforces a 512 KB file size limit and performs JSON parsing with schema checks. On I/O or parse errors, throws exceptions; when running as root, JSON parse error details are intentionally suppressed for security. Note: despite an error message string referring to a boolean, app_start_command is validated as a string in the implementation.
requirements: appRoot must be a valid filesystem path to an application root directory; the function will look for the file at <appRoot>/Passengerfile.json.

Caller must be prepared to handle exceptions: FileSystemException on open/read errors (other than ENOENT), SecurityException if the file exceeds 512 KB, and RuntimeException on JSON parse or schema validation errors (top-level must be an object; app_start_command must be a string if present; app_supports_kuria_protocol must be a boolean if present).
If the effective user ID is root, JSON parse error messages are suppressed; callers should not rely on detailed error strings in that case.
Behavior when the file is missing: the function returns a default-initialized AppLocalConfig without throwing.
The function performs file I/O and JSON parsing; ensure the process has read permissions for <appRoot>/Passengerfile.json.

functions.name: oxt::setup_syscall_interruption_support
functions.description: Initializes global support for interrupting blocking system calls and C library calls made through oxt::syscalls. After calling this, the oxt::syscalls wrappers act as interruption points and will throw boost::thread_interrupted when the calling thread is interrupted via oxt::thread::interrupt() or oxt::thread::interrupt_and_join().
requirements: Must be called before relying on interruption behavior of functions in oxt::syscalls.
Callers should be prepared to handle boost::thread_interrupted thrown from oxt::syscalls wrappers after this is enabled.
If system call interruption is disabled in the current scope (via boost::this_thread::disable_syscall_interruption), wrappers will not throw and will internally retry on EINTR.

functions.name: oxt::setup_random_failure_simulation
functions.description: Initializes random failure simulation for the oxt wrappers using a list of error probabilities. Intended for testing robustness by injecting failures according to the provided chances. Details of when/how failures are injected are not documented in this header.
requirements: errorChances must point to an array of n elements of oxt::ErrorChance.
n must be less than or equal to OXT_MAX_ERROR_CHANCES (16).
Each ErrorChance entry should contain a probability (double) and an error code (int); exact valid ranges/semantics beyond that are not specified here.
Callers should expect wrapper calls may simulate failures after initialization.

functions.name: oxt::syscalls::open
functions.description: Drop-in wrapper for POSIX open(path, oflag). Behaves like open but is an interruption point and may throw boost::thread_interrupted when the calling thread is interrupted (after interruption support is set up).
requirements: setup_syscall_interruption_support() should be called to enable interruption behavior.
path must be a valid, NUL-terminated filesystem path.
oflag must be a valid combination of open() flags as per POSIX.
Caller must handle possible boost::thread_interrupted exceptions.
When interruption is disabled in the current scope, the wrapper retries on EINTR and will not throw.

functions.name: oxt::syscalls::open
functions.signature: int oxt::syscalls::open(const char *path, int oflag, mode_t mode);
functions.description: Drop-in wrapper for POSIX open(path, oflag, mode). Same as open with mode when creating files; acts as an interruption point and may throw boost::thread_interrupted.
requirements: setup_syscall_interruption_support() should be called to enable interruption behavior.
path must be a valid, NUL-terminated filesystem path.

functions.name: oxt::thread::interrupt
functions.description: Requests interruption of the thread. Behaves like boost::thread::interrupt(), and if interruptSyscalls is true, interruption points in oxt::syscalls are also respected. Interruption requests can be missed depending on execution point; callers typically loop until a goal condition is satisfied.
requirements: The target must refer to a valid thread of execution created by oxt::thread.
If interruption needs to be guaranteed eventually, callers should issue repeated interrupts until completion, as a single request can be lost (per documentation).

requirements: May throw boost::thread_interrupted if the calling thread is interrupted before the join completes; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.
The oxt::thread object should represent a joinable thread; behavior follows boost::thread::join semantics when already joined or not-a-thread.

functions.description: Interrupts a set of threads and joins them efficiently by first issuing interrupts to all, then repeatedly joining any that become joinable until all are joined. Optionally respects interruption points in oxt::syscalls.
requirements: threads must point to an array with at least size elements.
Each threads[i] pointer must be non-null and point to a valid oxt::thread instance.
May throw boost::thread_interrupted if the calling thread is interrupted before all threads are joined; callers must handle this exception.

functions.description: RAII destructor that releases the held TimedLockable by calling unlock(). The corresponding constructor acquires the lock by repeatedly calling timed_lock with brief waits and interruption points, so destruction ensures the lock is released.
requirements: The associated TimedLockable must support unlock() and must be the same object that was successfully locked in the constructor.
Destructor must be called exactly once per instance (RAII); typically occurs automatically at end of scope.
Must be destroyed on the same thread that acquired the lock if the underlying TimedLockable requires same-thread unlocking (common for many mutex types).

functions.description: Constructs an empty dynamic thread group. Initializes internal bookkeeping so that threads created via create_thread() are tracked and will be interrupted and joined on destruction.

functions.name: oxt::dynamic_thread_group::~dynamic_thread_group
functions.description: Destructor for the dynamic thread group. Ensures all threads in the group are interrupted and joined by calling interrupt_and_join_all() before the group is destroyed, so threads do not outlive the group.

functions.name: oxt::dynamic_thread_group::create_thread
functions.signature: void oxt::dynamic_thread_group::create_thread(const boost::function<void ()>& func, const std::string& name = "", unsigned int stack_size = 0)
functions.description: Creates a new oxt::thread that runs the provided entry function and adds it to this group. The thread is named (auto-generated if name is empty) and may use a specified stack size (0 means use the system default). On failure to create a thread, throws thread_resource_error. On success, the group’s thread count increases by one and the thread is automatically removed from the group when it terminates.
requirements: > func must be a valid callable target compatible with signature void().
> If name is an empty string, an auto-generated name will be used (explicit behavior per documentation).
> If stack_size is 0, the system default stack size will be used.
> Caller must be prepared to handle thread_resource_error on failure to create the thread.

functions.name: oxt::dynamic_thread_group::interrupt_all
functions.description: Requests interruption of all threads currently in the group by invoking interrupt() on each. This does not join the threads; they continue to run until they finish or observe the interruption and exit.

functions.name: oxt::dynamic_thread_group::interrupt_and_join_all
functions.description: Interrupts all threads in the group and then joins them, waiting for completion. After return, the group is empty (postcondition: num_threads() == 0). The interruptSyscalls flag is forwarded to the underlying join logic to control interruption of blocking system calls.
requirements: > After this call returns, the group will contain no threads (postcondition).
> Safe to call even if there are zero threads (handles empty set).

functions.name: oxt::dynamic_thread_group::join_all
functions.description: Joins all threads currently in the group without first interrupting them. Waits for each to complete. After return, the group is empty (postcondition: num_threads() == 0).
requirements: > After this call returns, the group will contain no threads (postcondition).
> Safe to call even if there are zero threads (handles empty set).

functions.name: oxt::dynamic_thread_group::num_threads
functions.description: Returns the current number of threads being tracked in this group. Thread-safe; acquires an internal mutex to read the count.

functions.name: oxt::initialize
functions.description: Initializes the OXT (OS eXtensions for boosT) library so that dependent functionality works properly. This call sets up internal resources required by OXT. It does not enable system call interruption; call setup_syscall_interruption_support() separately if needed. Typical usage is to invoke this early during program startup before using OXT-dependent components.
requirements: Must be called before using features or components that depend on OXT being initialized.
Does not enable system call interruption; callers that require that behavior must also call setup_syscall_interruption_support().
Behavior on multiple or concurrent calls is unknown from this header; do not assume idempotency or thread-safety without further documentation.

functions.name: oxt::shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down OXT and frees resources that were allocated by oxt::initialize(). Typical usage is to call this during program shutdown after all OXT-dependent operations have completed.
requirements: Should be called only after a prior successful call to oxt::initialize().
Call only after all OXT-dependent operations have finished, as it frees resources used by OXT.
Behavior on multiple or concurrent calls is unknown from this header; do not assume it is safe to call more than once or from multiple threads without further documentation.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: null-terminated C string
# We must produce bytes that represent interesting, valid C strings
# to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR()/c_str() in the fuzzers, which
# concatenate with Passenger::StaticString. Embedded NULs would cause
# early truncation by strlen, so avoid interior NULs. Always end with a single NUL.
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = (
    string.ascii_lowercase + string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits +
    " _-./:@,%+?=&~#[](){}$^*!'\"\\|;<>`\t\r\n"
)

SHELL_METAS = [
    "*", "?", "[abc]", "$(whoami)", "`uname -a`", "|", ";", "&&", "||",
    "\"quoted with spaces\"", "'single quoted'", "\\"  # backslash only
]

XML_SPECIALS = ["<", ">", "&", "\"", "'"]

PATHY_SEGMENTS = [
    "/", "./", "../", "/tmp/", "/var/log/", "/home/user/", "C:/Windows/", "\\\\server\\share\\",
]

URLY_SEGMENTS = [
    "http://", "https://", "file://", "unix://", "ssh://", "ws://", "wss://",
]

MODE_STRINGS = [
    "u=rwx,g=rx,o=rx", "u=rw,g=r,o=",
    "u=rwxs,g=rx,o=x",  # includes s for user/group
]

EDGE_CASES = [
    "",  # empty string
    " ",
    "\t\n\r",
    ".", "..",
    "0", "1", "-1", "+1",
    "false", "true", "null", "None",
]

REPETITIVE = [
    "a" * 1,
    "a" * 8,
    "a" * 63,
    "A" * 128,
    "Z" * 1024,
]

HEX_CHARS = string.hexdigits.lower()

def rnd(r: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return r.choice(seq)

def make_ascii_block(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def make_hex(r: random.Random, nbytes: int) -> str:
    # 2 hex chars per byte
    return ''.join(r.choice(HEX_CHARS) for _ in range(nbytes * 2))

def make_urlish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rnd(r, URLY_SEGMENTS)
    host = make_ascii_block(r, 3, 10).replace(" ", "").replace("/", "")
    path = '/' + make_ascii_block(r, 0, 10).replace(' ', '%20')
    return base + host + path

def make_pathish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    p = rnd(r, PATHY_SEGMENTS)
    segs = [make_ascii_block(r, 1, 6).replace('/', '_') for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3))]
    return p + "/".join(segs)

def make_shellish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    k = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(k):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(make_ascii_block(r, 1, 8))
        else:
            parts.append(rnd(r, SHELL_METAS))
    return ' '.join(parts)

def make_xmlish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    core = make_ascii_block(r, 3, 12)
    insert = rnd(r, XML_SPECIALS)
    tail = make_ascii_block(r, 0, 8)
    return core + insert + tail

def assemble_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands = []
    # Edge cases and small tokens
    cands.extend(EDGE_CASES)
    cands.extend(REPETITIVE)

    # Path/URL-like strings
    for _ in range(3):
        cands.append(make_pathish(r))
        cands.append(make_urlish(r))

    # Shell-like, XML-like, and mode strings
    for _ in range(3):
        cands.append(make_shellish(r))
        cands.append(make_xmlish(r))
    cands.extend(MODE_STRINGS)

    # Hex strings of varying sizes
    cands.append(make_hex(r, 4))
    cands.append(make_hex(r, 16))

    # Mixed alphanumeric with punctuation
    for _ in range(5):
        cands.append(make_ascii_block(r, 1, 40))

    # Combine segments to reach larger sizes but keep under 4096
    big = []
    total_len = 0
    while total_len < 1500 and len(big) < 40:
        part = rnd(r, cands)
        big.append(part)
        total_len += len(part) + 1
    cands.append(' '.join(big))

    return cands

def to_c_string(data: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure there are no interior NULs and append exactly one terminating NUL.
    # Replace any accidental NULs with spaces to keep it valid.
    sanitized = data.replace('\x00', ' ')
    b = sanitized.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    # Truncate to leave space for terminator under 4096
    if len(b) >= 4095:
        b = b[:4095]
    return b + b"\x00"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    cands = assemble_candidates(r)

    # Choose a strategy for final output
    strategy = r.random()
    if strategy < 0.2:
        # Single candidate
        s = rnd(r, cands)
        return to_c_string(s)
    elif strategy < 0.6:
        # Concatenate two to exercise operator+ length math with diverse sizes
        a = rnd(r, cands)
        b = rnd(r, cands)
        return to_c_string(a + b)
    else:
        # Build a structured composite mimicking command + args or path + query
        parts = []
        parts.append(rnd(r, URLY_SEGMENTS + PATHY_SEGMENTS))
        parts.append(make_ascii_block(r, 3, 12))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append('?')
            # query k=v&k2=v2 style
            n = r.randint(1, 4)
            kvs = []
            for _ in range(n):
                k = make_ascii_block(r, 1, 6).replace(' ', '+')
                v = make_ascii_block(r, 0, 8).replace(' ', '+')
                kvs.append(f"{k}={v}")
            parts.append('&'.join(kvs))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append('#')
            parts.append(make_ascii_block(r, 1, 8))
        s = ''.join(parts)
        return to_c_string(s)

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate arbitrary byte strings intended to be fed into FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Targeted behaviors for StaticString vs std::string comparisons:
# - Empty, short ASCII, long ASCII
# - Binary with NULs
# - Repeated patterns and prefixes/suffixes
# - Unicode UTF-8 sequences
# - Strings that differ by last byte
# The buffer encodes a sequence of test cases so the fuzzer can pull many different lhs strings.
#
# Encoding format:
# [u16 count][ entries... ] where each entry is [u16 length][data...]
# This mirrors common corpus formats and is easy to parse by the stub harness.
# We keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<H", n & 0xFFFF)


def _clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return max(lo, min(hi, n))


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _utf8_samples() -> List[bytes]:
    # A small set of valid UTF-8 sequences to exercise multi-byte comparisons
    return [
        "".encode("utf-8"),
        "hello".encode("utf-8"),
        "héllo".encode("utf-8"),
        "こんにちは".encode("utf-8"),
        "🙂".encode("utf-8"),
        "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢".encode("utf-8"),
    ]


def _build_entries(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty
    entries.append(b"")

    # 2) Short ASCII
    entries.extend([
        b"a",
        b"abc",
        b"ABC",
        b"AaBbCc",
        b"0",
        b"1234567890",
    ])

    # 3) With NULs and binary data
    entries.extend([
        b"\x00",
        b"\x00\x00\x00",
        b"abc\x00def",
        b"\xFF\xFE\xFD\xFC",
        b"bin\x00\xFF\x00ary",
    ])

    # 4) Prefix/suffix pairs (to compare equal prefixes with different lengths)
    base = b"prefix-common-"
    entries.extend([
        base,
        base + b"A",
        base + b"B",
        base + b"A" * 16,
    ])

    # 5) Repeated patterns
    pat = b"xyz"
    entries.append(pat * rng.randrange(1, 20))

    # 6) Random ASCII varying lengths
    for _ in range(6):
        n = rng.randrange(0, 64)
        entries.append(_rand_ascii(rng, n))

    # 7) Random binary including NULs
    for _ in range(6):
        n = rng.randrange(0, 64)
        entries.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n))

    # 8) UTF-8 samples
    entries.extend(_utf8_samples())

    # 9) Long strings to exercise memcmp long-path and hashing loops
    long1 = _rand_ascii(rng, 512)
    long2 = long1[:-1] + bytes([long1[-1] ^ 0x01]) if long1 else b"X"  # differ by last byte
    long3 = _rand_bytes(rng, 1024)
    entries.extend([long1, long2, long3])

    # 10) Hex-like and shell-sensitive strings
    entries.extend([
        b"deadbeef",
        b"$PATH",
        b"--option=value",
        b"a b\tc\nd",
        b"quote'" + b"x" * 5 + b"\"double\"",
        b"<xml>&\"'",
    ])

    # 11) Mode string grammar candidates to pair with parseModeString elsewhere
    entries.extend([
        b"u=rwx,g=rx,o=",
        b"u=rw,g=w,o=rx",
        b"u=rs,g=rw,o=x",
        b"g=rw",
    ])

    # 12) Similar strings differing early vs late
    s = _rand_ascii(rng, 64)
    entries.extend([
        s,
        (bytes([s[0] ^ 1]) + s[1:]) if s else b"",
        (s[:-1] + bytes([s[-1] ^ 1])) if s else b"",
    ])

    # Shuffle to mix deterministic and random
    rng.shuffle(entries)

    return entries


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    entries = _build_entries(rng)

    # Pack into length-prefixed list with u16 count and u16 lengths.
    out = bytearray()
    # Reserve space: we'll compute allowed entries within MAX_TOTAL
    # First, estimate header size (2 bytes for count) plus each entry adds 2 + len
    out.extend(_u16(0))  # placeholder for count

    count = 0
    for e in entries:
        # ensure individual entry length fits u16
        if len(e) > 0xFFFF:
            e = e[:0xFFFF]
        needed = 2 + len(e)
        if len(out) + needed > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(_u16(len(e)))
        out.extend(e)
        count += 1

    # Write count
    out[0:2] = _u16(count)

    return bytes(out)
